note: About as close to the stated ICP as this corpus gets: a 51-year-old dentist running multiple businesses, lifelong athlete, already training three times a week and already using kettlebells, who framed the purchase in exactly the language of the ICP — "I'm not fat, I'm not out of shape right now, but I know I could do so much better... I'm just ready to take it to the next level." Health is the neglected corner of an otherwise successful life, not a crisis. Income is a match on capacity rather than on liquidity: he described business expenditures in the tens of thousands a month but real cash-flow pressure this cycle, which is the same pattern the ICP observations flag as being solved by a payment plan rather than by screening. I have logged not_deconditioned as a miss, not because he is deconditioned — he plainly is not — but because the criterion is the exclusion test and the thing that should have excluded or gated him here is clinical: a lumbar flare-up four years ago serious enough to need epidural injections, and a physician's directive about what he should and should not train. The stated ICP has no clinical criterion, so a prospect with a spinal history reads as core fit on every screen the company actually applies.
